subject_identity_preserved.rationale: Shots 0-4 repeatedly show an olive-drab helicopter and military-deck/airfield activity, but human identities are unstable and the aircraft begins morphing/overlaying. Shots 5-6 switch to a cockpit/airborne view with a different helicopter focus, so the original central helicopter-and-two-men subject is no longer preserved.

background_coherent.rationale: The early shots keep a plausible deck or airfield setting around the same helicopter, but shots 4-6 transition into airborne terrain/cockpit imagery. The scene no longer remains the same place or event.

per_shot_adherence.issue: Matches the outdoor olive-drab helicopter and shirtless crew activity, though the uniformed man is unclear and the vintage look is not especially archival.
Maintains the helicopter/deck invariant with two shirtless men, but does not match the described indoor workshop or single mechanic caption.
Does not follow the close-up rotor/weather-vane caption; it remains on the helicopter side with people and a foreground pole obstruction.
Still shows the same helicopter exterior, but not an aerial ship-deck takeoff; there are ghosted compositing artifacts and no clear lift-off.
Partially suggests multiple helicopters and landscape, but is dominated by a translucent overlay of the prior helicopter and lacks clean formation-flight composition.
Adheres well to the cockpit/pilot silhouette with another helicopter visible outside, but breaks the maintained airfield/deck invariant.
Shows an airborne helicopter over terrain through an aircraft window, matching much of the caption, but not the same original helicopter and crew setting.

inter_shot_diversity.rationale: The sequence contains varied exterior, deck, cockpit, and airborne views with different compositions and actions. Some diversity is caused by identity drift rather than legitimate continuity, but it is not collapsed to a copied shot.

motion_continuity.rationale: There is visible progression from crew activity around the helicopter to flight/cockpit views, with moving figures, rotors, and changing viewpoints. However, several transitions look like abrupt crossfades or subject swaps rather than smooth continuous action.

which_cut_broke.how: The transition from shot 4 to shot 5 most clearly abandons the original exterior helicopter/deck scene and crew, switching to a cockpit silhouette and airborne operation.

cheat_flags.rationale: Frames are not copied or frozen, and the model attempts different requested views. The main failure is consistency drift and ghosted blending, not a collapse cheat.
